whatTheseAre: The terminal SCREEN codex draws when `/rename` is typed at the composer and confirmed
with Return — the `/rename` modal, captured to answer one question Task 0/1 of the
'type /rename into a live codex TUI' plan exists to settle: whether `▌` (U+258C, LEFT HALF
BLOCK) is the FIRST character of its line inside the
requires, or whether it sits behind indentation/box-drawing the way a naive port of that
check would miss. This is the codex counterpart of the `tui.captured.provenance.json` set
one level up in intent — same capture route, same pyte renderer — but where those five
cover the composer/dialog shapes already reasoned about, this one is new ground: no
capture of the rename modal existed anywhere in the repo before this task.
environmentNote: codex --version  -> codex-cli 0.154.0 (the standing tui.captured.provenance.json set was
taken at 0.148.0; codex has shipped several releases since — the
composer box in this capture is narrower, 52 columns not 45, and adds
an MCP-startup-issue line and a 'fast' mode tag neither older capture
has, so treat this as its own baseline, not a diff against those five)
~/.codex/auth.json present, mode 0600 — the operator's real, personal codex home was used
for this capture (not an isolated CODEX_HOME with a throwaway config, unlike the five-file
set), because the task specified an exact, real, already-finished thread id to resume:
01a08bf2-c01e-7720-baa8-57c776501c24. Nothing was sent to the model: /rename is a local TUI
command, never a prompt, and the two hard constraints in the task brief (never type a name;
capture with display(), never dump()) were both honored.
glyphs: **The modal's marker is `▌` (U+258C, LEFT HALF BLOCK), and it is a THIRD glyph in the
family documented by tui.captured.provenance.json's `glyphs` — distinct from both:
claude's input box and dialog cursor   ❯   U+276F   HEAVY RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION
codex's composer box and dialog cursor ›   U+203A   SINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION
codex's /rename modal's left rule      ▌   U+258C   LEFT HALF BLOCK
It is NOT `›` printed differently — it is a different codepoint, confirmed by direct
content search of the raw capture: `›` does not occur anywhere on screen while the modal
is up (see verdicts.markerIsLineLeading below). `InputBar.read`'s marker constant would need
a THIRD case to recognize this screen at all; it is not a widening of the codex-composer
case, because on this screen the composer itself is not drawn — the modal replaces it.
capturedBy: One real `codex resume 01a08bf2-c01e-7720-baa8-57c776501c24` session in a pty owned by the
capture harness, 136x45, TERM default (pexpect's pty, no TERM override), rendered from the
pty byte stream by pyte 0.8.2 (installed in a throwaway venv, not system python) via a
task's hard constraint — `dump()` prefixes line numbers that would themselves become
`$0.first`) and written with per-line trailing whitespace stripped, `\n`-joined, exactly as
the five-file precedent set describes its own route.
Sequence: spawn `codex resume <id>`, wait ~6s. The FIRST screen was not the composer — it
was a 'Choose working directory to resume this session' dialog (this worktree's cwd differs
from the thread's recorded cwd), which the probe answered with a bare Return to accept its
default-highlighted option ('Use session directory'), never a typed digit or name. Waited
~3s more for the real composer, confirmed by the literal string 'Ask Codex to do anything'
on screen (NOT by the presence of the marker glyph alone — a first version of the probe
checked only `line.lstrip().startswith('›')` and false-positived on the workdir dialog's
own '› 1. Use session directory' row, which carries the identical glyph). Sent the literal
keystrokes '/rename' then a bare '\r', waited ~2s more for the lazy repaint, then captured.
Sent Escape, confirmed the modal closed back to the composer, then terminated the child.
No other keys were sent at any point; no name was ever typed.
writerLock: Not probed here — out of scope for this task. See tui.captured.provenance.json's own
writerLock section for the measurement that /rename's app-server path is what has to carry
the write instead of a live TUI keystroke, which is the reason this whole plan exists.

markerIsLineLeading: YES — confirmed by direct inspection of the raw pyte grid (character-by-character, not
just the joined string), on the SAME row that carries the modal's title:
row 19  col 0 = '▌'  (fg 00cdcd, not bold)   -- the modal's left rule / title row
row 20  col 0 = '▌'  (fg 00cdcd, not bold)   -- a rule-only row, blank otherwise
row 21  col 0 = '▌'  (fg 00cdcd, not bold)   -- the rule / input-value row
repr() of the exact raw line (before scrubbing; scrubbing only ever touched the composer
box's 'directory:' line, several rows above the modal and untouched here):
`line[0] == '▌'` is true with zero leading whitespace or box-drawing before it — there is
no indentation, no outer box character, nothing between column 0 and the marker. This is
the opposite shape from `ChoiceDialog`'s box-drawn dialogs (workspace-trust.captured.txt,
approval-command.captured.txt), which sit inside a `│ ... │` frame with the option marker
one or two columns in; the /rename modal draws no surrounding box at all, just three
`▌`-ruled rows flush against the left edge of the terminal.

Row 20 is the marker alone on a blank rule — there is no text between the two content

Footer (row 23, NOT marker-prefixed, default colour): 'Press enter to confirm or esc to go
back' — a different footer text from both of workspace-trust's 'Press enter to continue'
and approval-command's 'Press enter to confirm or esc to cancel'; this one alone says

composerMarkerAbsentUnderModal: CONFIRMED absent. Direct substring search of the raw 45-row capture for '›' (U+203A, the
codex composer/dialog marker) returns zero occurrences anywhere on screen while the modal
is up. The composer box, its placeholder, and the status footer line below it ('gpt-5.6-sol
default fast · ... · session 2') are all gone — the modal fully replaces that region of the
screen rather than overlaying or coexisting with it. A reader that scans for '›' to decide
whether the composer is present would correctly report it is NOT, while a reader using ONLY
'first character is a marker glyph' without also checking WHICH glyph would misidentify the
modal's own rows as a composer line, since both are genuinely `$0.first == <some marker>`.

editingRule: Lines may be DROPPED, never EDITED — with one deliberate, documented exception in this
file: the composer box's 'directory: <path>' row (row 5) had its real value
(`/tmp/fd-codex-untrusted-<hex>`, the resumed thread's actual recorded throwaway workdir)
replaced with the neutral placeholder `/tmp/work`, matching tui-idle.captured.txt's own
convention. This is scrubbing, not tidying: the SAME box-fixed-width alignment was
preserved by construction — the replacement path was right-padded with spaces so the row's
total length and the column of the closing `│` are byte-identical to the unscrubbed row, not
a naive find-and-replace that would have shifted the border out of alignment with the other
four box rows. No other line in this file needed scrubbing: `rg -n
All 45 rows of the 45-row grid are present, blank rows included, exactly as captured — the

Whether `▌`'s row-21 value ('session 2') is genuinely rendered as a placeholder hint
(colour-distinguished from a real draft, the way the composer's 'Ask Codex to do anything'

The modal after a real edit — e.g. after typing a replacement character or two, or after

A /rename modal opened on a thread that ALREADY has a custom (non-default) name — this
thread's row-21 value was codex's own auto-generated 'session 2' label; whether a
previously-renamed thread's modal opens with that custom name pre-filled the same way is
unmeasured.
Any width narrower than 136 columns. Untested whether the modal's fixed-width composer box
above it (52 columns wide at this capture) reflows, and whether the `▌`-ruled rows wrap a
long custom name onto a continuation line.
A capture under `TERM=xterm-ghostty`, which the five-file precedent set used explicitly.
This probe ran under pexpect's default inherited TERM instead (recorded in capturedBy). TUI
programs can branch glyph and colour decisions on TERM, so this is an uncontrolled variable
relative to the established capture route. Nothing here suggests TERM affected the rows this
fixture is evidence for — the marker's column-0 position is structural, not a rendering
choice — but the variable was not held constant, and that belongs in this list rather than
left implicit.
